findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls timezone.now() when the dataclass class is defined, not when an instance is created. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued value therefore shares the process import timestamp. If queued is intended to record when an assignment was queued (e.g. for future staleness/debouncing checks or observability), it will be wrong by however long the process has been running. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now) instead.

findings.title: to_dict() puts a raw datetime into Celery task kwargs, breaking the round-trip
findings.body: assignment_source.to_dict() uses dataclasses.asdict(), so the `queued` value passed in the sync_assignee_outbound Celery kwargs is a datetime object, not a JSON-native value. Sentry Celery tasks serialize kwargs as JSON, so enqueueing can fail with a serialization error on exactly the inbound-assignment path this PR enables (propagating synchronously out of GroupAssignee.assign/deassign via sync_group_assignee_outbound), and where a serializer does coerce datetimes it arrives at AssignmentSource.from_dict as a string, silently violating the declared datetime type since from_dict performs no parsing/validation. Serialize queued to an ISO string in to_dict and parse it back in from_dict, or drop it from the wire format; the added tests use eager tasks and a direct to_dict assertion, so they never exercise this round-trip.

findings.title: Task unconditionally passes new assignment_source kwarg to all installations
findings.body: sync_assignee_outbound now always calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source), even when it is None, while the abstract IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound signature was not updated to declare this parameter (it still only documents **kwargs). Any installation whose concrete sync_assignee_outbound does not accept **kwargs/an assignment_source parameter will raise TypeError at runtime, causing the task to retry and the outbound sync to fail; the new test mocks ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound, which accepts arbitrary kwargs, so it cannot catch such an incompatibility. Either declare the parameter on the abstract method and update implementations, or only pass it when supported/non-None.

findings.title: No test for deassign suppression or for propagation to a different integration
findings.body: The only cycle-suppression test covers assign() where the source integration matches the single linked integration, asserting the outbound call is skipped. There is no equivalent test for deassign() with a matching AssignmentSource, and no test where an assignment sourced from one integration still syncs outbound to a different linked integration, which is the behavior the should_sync comment claims to preserve. A regression that suppresses all outbound syncs whenever any assignment_source is present, or that fails to suppress deassign cycles, would pass the current suite.
